citations.title: NCDOR Sales and Use Tax Bulletins (January 2026), SUTB 72-4A.2, Services to Multiple Like-Kind Items

citations.quote: The bathroom update does not meet the definition of “remodeling” and is taxable as repair, maintenance, and installation services because the true purpose is the service of replacing the prefabricate fiberglass shower enclosure.

notes: The contractor must substantiate a capital improvement (Form E-589CI); otherwise services to real property are presumed taxable repair, maintenance and installation. summary: North Carolina taxes only tangible property, certain digital property and a short list of specified services; professional services are not among them.

citations.title: NCDOR, Taxable Items (Overview of Sales and Use Taxes)
citations.quote: North Carolina imposes sales and use tax on the sales price of, or gross receipts derived from, taxable sales of the following:

citations.title: NCDOR, Taxable Items (Overview of Sales and Use Taxes)
citations.quote: The following services and items are subject to sales and use tax:

notes: Covers service.professional.other (and any subcode without its own rule). The NCDOR overview says North Carolina imposes the tax on taxable sales of three things (tangible personal property, certain digital property, and 'specified services') and lists the specified services: admissions, dry cleaning and laundry, leases and rentals, prepaid calling, real property contracts, accommodations, repair, maintenance and installation services, satellite radio, service contracts, telecommunications and video programming. No professional service is among them; the page does not use the word 'only', but the imposition sentence names the whole base. The overview's wording dates from a 2026 redesign (Wayback copies through 2024 are a link list), and SUTB is the 01/01/2026 edition, so the rule starts 2026-01-01; the treatment is older (the RMI services regime dates from 2016-03-01) but earlier evidence was not gathered. A professional charge billed by a retailer as part of a taxable sale, not separately stated, is part of the sales price (G.S. 105-164.3). Made conditional 2026-11-01: a professional service of a kind no subcode names may be one the law enumerates as taxable (dev case ia-11, Iowa investment counseling). 2026-11-02: cited page moved from https://www.ncdor.gov/taxes-forms/sales-and-use-tax/overview-sales-and-use-taxes to https://www.ncdor.gov/taxes-forms/sales-and-use-tax/taxable-items.

notes: North Carolina taxes qualifying food at a 2.00% local rate only: the county's general local sales taxes (Articles 39, 40 and 42) apply to it and the transit and other local taxes (e.g. Articles 43 and 46) don't.
